solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tangle between rival gangs

indicators.note: the letters sit between the ends of the words rival and gangs, straddling the gap between them

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out between two rival street gangs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangle' looks like a scuffle between the gangs, but it is a noun naming a kind of seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for large seaweeds such as kelp, which are a type of alga.

clue.text: Spanish region with a Latin institute in America

parts.note: and means with, together with

indicators.note: the institute is placed in America

parts.note: USA is America

explanation.surface: A Spanish region with a Latin institute based in America.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the large southern autonomous community of Spain, home to Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Moan about investing money in food — the Parisian style

indicators.note: the food invests, i.e. clothes or surrounds, the money

parts.note: grub is slang for food
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Complaining about putting money into food, French style.
explanation.definitionFit: To moan is to complain, a straightforward synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Toddler is an example of one finally asleep in cot

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the cot, i.e. inside the word for it

parts.note: a cot is a child's bed
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of asleep

explanation.surface: A toddler is an example of a child that finally falls asleep in its cot.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler walks on two legs, so it is one instance of a two-footed creature.

clue.text: Busy person needs to sort out vegetables

parts.note: busy as a bee, so a bee is a busy person

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A busy person needs to sort out the vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort out' reads as one phrase, but 'to sort' is the fodder and 'out' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These are red root vegetables, eaten boiled or pickled.

clue.text: Punctilious, quaint, picky, quirky? No doubt you'll mind these!

definitions.text: Punctilious, quaint, picky, quirky? No doubt you'll mind these!

parts.words: Punctilious, quaint, picky, quirky? No doubt you'll mind these!
parts.note: the four words are themselves words starting with P and Q, and minding those letters means being careful of manners

explanation.surface: A list of fussy adjectives for a careful person.
explanation.walkthrough: Punctilious and picky start with P, quaint and quirky with Q; 'mind your Ps and Qs' means watch your manners.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom refers to good manners and etiquette, things a polite person is careful about.

clue.text: Tears produced by taking up violin

indicators.note: in a down clue taking up means lifting, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: Tears shed on taking up the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' suggests crying but is the verb to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear is to rush along, and to dart is likewise to move fast.

clue.text: High rise shown by northern rent

parts.note: a tor is a high rocky hill, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: A tower block in the north where rents are charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High rise' suggests a tower block and 'rent' money paid, but rent here is a past participle meaning ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent as an adjective means ripped apart, a synonym of the participle for tearing.

clue.text: Programmes allow retired actors to cut directions

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to let is to allow

indicators.note: the actors cut into the directions, splitting them

parts.note: E and S are compass directions, east and south
a cast is a company of actors

explanation.surface: Programmes allowing retired actors to cut the stage directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Television broadcasts are programmes shown on screen.

clue.text: Not good for environmentalist to exert force to establish law a second time

indicators.note: not good means without the letter for good, so it is removed

parts.note: a Green is an environmental campaigner
to act is to exert force or have an effect

explanation.surface: A bad environmentalist exerts force to re-establish a law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'law' looks like part of the wordplay giving ACT, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a law again is to make it statute once more, the legislative sense.

clue.text: Initially 10 led 9 rebel astray like Day-Lewis

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the answer to clue 10
letters gone astray have wandered out of order, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to clue 9 is the word for work or childbirth, the party name

explanation.surface: Like a Labour rebel led astray, which ties loosely to the actor Day-Lewis.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 is DUSTCOAT, whose first letter D starts the answer; the 9 is LABOUR, shuffled with LED and REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Day-Lewis has a hyphenated two-part surname, which is what a double-barrelled name is.

clue.text: What mothers have been through work?

definitions.meaning: the process of childbirth, which every mother has endured
toil or effort, as a noun

explanation.surface: Is childbirth really a form of work, the question asks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the process of giving birth and hard physical work.

clue.text: Overall, perhaps, you would wear one to avoid getting one

definitions.text: Overall, perhaps, you would wear one to avoid getting one

parts.words: Overall, perhaps, you would wear one to avoid getting one
parts.note: a protective coat worn to keep off dust; the second 'one' is a coat of dust on your clothes

explanation.surface: A riddle about wearing a garment to avoid getting covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overall' looks like 'on the whole' but is the garment; the second 'one' is a coating of dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A light protective coat worn over clothes is a kind of overall, keeping grime off.

clue.text: Misleading details about debt

indicators.note: the word for details goes about, i.e. around, the debt

parts.note: specs, short for specifications, are details
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of debt

explanation.surface: Details given about a debt are misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means plausible on the surface but actually false, hence deceptive.

clue.text: Strut about ring in high spirits

parts.note: to cock is to strut or swagger like a cockerel
a is an old preposition meaning on or about, as in a-hunting
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: Strutting around a ring full of confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means exultant and boastfully pleased, a synonym of elated.

clue.text: Old money advanced to join exercise group

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a set is a group
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Old money has been advanced to join an exercise group.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was Spain's currency before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Irreverently disrupted replay of gripping National

indicators.note: the rearranged letters grip, hold within them, the national abbreviation
disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Swearing irreverently at a disrupted replay of a gripping Grand National.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' makes PROFAELY, and 'gripping' puts N inside it; 'National' looks like the horse race but is only the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting profanely means showing disrespect toward sacred things, i.e. without reverence.

clue.text: Strangely it updates natural abilities

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: Oddly, it upgrades a person's natural talents.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptitudes are innate talents or flairs for doing things.

clue.text: What was counted on from a graduate course, oddly

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in odd positions of course

explanation.surface: Something that a graduate course could once rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counted on' looks like 'relied on' but means literally used for counting.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires was the device people did arithmetic on.

clue.text: Fifties dropout's exhausted family flips

parts.note: beat means tired out

indicators.note: flips means turns over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: kin are family

explanation.surface: A 1950s dropout is tired and his family turns against him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flips' looks like losing one's temper but turns KIN round.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Beat Generation of the 1950s rejected conventional society, a dropout.

clue.text: Sign of heraldry with Queen in closest buckles

indicators.note: the queen is placed in the rearranged word
something that buckles bends out of shape, so the letters of closest are reshaped

parts.note: R, for Regina, stands for queen

explanation.surface: A heraldic sign of the Queen in the closest buckles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckles' looks like belt fasteners but is a verb rearranging CLOSEST into COSSLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cross whose arms end in further crosses is a charge in coats of arms.

clue.text: Fellow leaves one city for another

indicators.note: the fellow leaves, departs from, the first city

parts.note: Manchester is a city in north-west England
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man moves from one city to another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'another' borrows 'city' from earlier in the clue: another city. Chester is a walled city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, so it is another English urban centre.

clue.text: Right cheek

definitions.meaning: a right or freedom, something one is entitled to

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a freedom or entitlement and presumptuous impudence.

clue.text: Suspend international union backing protecting artist's aggressive speech

indicators.note: the word for suspend wraps round, protecting, the artist

parts.note: to hang is to suspend
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; 's is a link

indicators.note: backing means the letters run backwards

parts.note: the EU, European Union, is an international union

explanation.surface: Halt international union support for an artist's aggressive address.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a lengthy, forceful and hostile tirade.

clue.text: Mature women will desert Take That, perhaps

indicators.note: the women desert, leaving the word for mature

parts.note: to grow up is to mature

explanation.surface: Grown-up women will abandon the boy band Take That.
explanation.walkthrough: Take That is a British boy band; 'Take That' looks like a command.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop band is a musical group, and Take That is one example.

clue.text: Almost everything's built without it in France

parts.note: all means everything; the 's is a link

indicators.note: without means the French word is taken out of built

parts.note: il is French for it

explanation.surface: Almost everything is built without it in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nearly or very nearly, as in being almost finished.

clue.text: Delighted when told foot op cast will wrap up right

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap up, enclosing, the letter for right
to cast is to throw, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient told their foot operation cast will wrap up properly is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a plaster cast; it rearranges WHEN TOLD FOOT OP, which wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being extremely happy and elated.

clue.text: Miss dance

definitions.meaning: to omit or pass over something
to move lightly with little hops

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to leave out or omit and to hop lightly as if dancing.

clue.text: Duck's hit over by railway

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: rap means hit

explanation.surface: A duck hit over by a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird but is the verb to dodge; 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To parry a blow is to ward it off or evade it, as one ducks.

clue.text: Scans MPs' votes according to Speaker

indicators.note: the word is as heard, as the Speaker of the Commons would call it

parts.note: ayes are votes in favour in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: The Speaker scans the votes of MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker chairs the UK House of Commons and announces the ayes and noes.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look it over, so the verb means scans.
